exposure: Dry powder (DP) synthetic lung surfactant (with phospholipids and Super Mini-B (SMB) peptide analogue)
outcome: In vitro surface activity (captive bubble surfactometry)
cohort: The study participants were surfactant-deficient adult rabbits and preterm lambs.
finding: Aerosol delivery of dry powder synthetic surfactant during non-invasive respiratory support with nCPAP significantly improved oxygenation and lung function in surfactant-deficient animals, and this response could be enhanced by giving a second dose.
